tasks.title: XKF4.SP from the position innovation
tasks.solution: test ratio = (y_N² + y_E²) / ((G/100)² · (S_N + S_E)) (AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp); XKF4.SP holds its square root. A value above 1 means the gate rejected the measurement.

tasks.title: The FS_EKF_THRESH threshold in sigmas
tasks.solution: A variance in XKF4 and in the GCS is |y| / ((G/100)·√S), that is the innovation as a fraction of the gate. A threshold T corresponds to an innovation of T · G/100 sigmas: 0.8 with a gate of 500 is 4σ, and with the compass gate of 300 it is 2.4σ.

tasks.title: EKF3 synthetic airspeed
tasks.solution: The wind triangle: v_air = v_ground − wind, TAS = |v_ground − wind| (AP_AHRS::_airspeed_EAS, the EKF3_SYNTHETIC branch; the vector is three-dimensional, but the EKF3 wind is horizontal, so with zero vertical velocity N and E are enough; outward the AHRS returns EAS = TAS / EAS2TAS). With AHRS_WIND_MAX > 0 the result is also constrained to ground speed ± that limit.

tasks.title: Dead reckoning error of a plane without GPS
tasks.solution: The wind at height h: W · √(h/60). The estimation error Δw = wind · p/100. With an airspeed sensor the airspeed is known, so the position drifts at the rate Δw: e ≈ Δw · t. The module's example: 8 · √(50/60) = 7.30 m/s, estimate 7.1, Δw = 0.2 m/s, 12 m in 60 s (11.5 m in SITL). Without a sensor the error grows faster than this formula gives.

tasks.title: Position drift from a tilt error
tasks.solution: A wrong tilt δθ turns part of g into a false horizontal acceleration a = g · sin δθ; uncorrected, the position drifts by ½ · a · t². At 0.5° and 10 s that is 4.3 m, which is why EKF3 declares the position lost after only 7–10 s without measurements.
